answer_1.quote: We present Plag-Bench, a large-scale corpus containing 46.5K text pairs with three plagiarism categories: verbatim, paraphrase, and summary plagiarism. These samples cover three writing domains (abstract of scholarly paper, story, news article) and are synthetically generated by three advanced ... LLMs ... to acquire the gold standard for automatic plagiarism detection tasks.
answer_1.outputs: paraphrased texts, summarized texts, plagiarism detection predictions

answer_2.quote: For paraphrase plagiarism, we perform an evaluation of LLM-paraphrased documents through the lens of semantic equivalence, consistency, and language quality... We use the source documents as reference documents and carefully choose a single representative metric for every aspect. • Semantic equivalence → BERTScore ... • Consistency → AlignScore ... • Language quality → Readability index & COLAScore. For summary evaluation we use BLANC, BARTScore, AlignScore, Readability index, etc.

answer_3.quote: We evaluate Five LLMs, Llama2-70b-chat, Llama3-70b-instruct, Mixtral-8x7B-instruct, GPT-3.5 Turbo, and GPT-4 Turbo, for binary classification of plagiarism and plagiarism type identification. We experiment with four popular prompting techniques: zero-shot vanilla prompting, zero-shot Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, few-shot vanilla prompting, and few-shot CoT prompting.

answer_4.quote: We use Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) to hire human annotators for three separate annotation tasks: non-plagiarism evaluation, paraphrase evaluation, and summary evaluation... Each sample ... we compute the inter-rater agreement scores... The final data contains ... samples for the plagiarism-free, paraphrase, and summary plagiarism labels.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators answer questions about plagiarism presence and, for paraphrase, assess semantic equivalence, consistency, and language quality; for summary, assess relevance, coherence, consistency, and language quality.
